questions.prompt: State what is meant by deformation and describe the restriction used for deformation in this lesson.
Which force arrangement places a straight wire in tension?

options.A: Both end forces point toward the centre of the wire.
options.B: Both end forces point away from the centre of the wire.
options.C: Both end forces point to the right.
options.D: No force acts at either end.

questions.prompt: A block has original length 50.0 mm and final length 49.4 mm. Which description is correct?
A bar has equal inward forces at its ends. What can be concluded?

options.C: The resultant force can be zero while the bar is compressed.

questions.prompt: A polymer strip has original length 0.250 m. An applied load changes its length to 0.257 m. Identify the type of loading, calculate the change in length, and explain the direction of the end forces.

figure.purpose: Assess interpretation of end-force direction and measured lengths
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line diagram of a strip beside a ruler, with original and final lengths labelled but no force arrows. The learner explains the required arrow directions in words.
figure.alt_text: A strip is shown at original and final lengths beside a ruler.

questions.prompt: A column is 1.200 m long before loading and 1.197 m long after loading. Calculate the compression. Then explain why equal opposite forces on the column may give no acceleration but still cause deformation.

Two objects are held stationary under equal opposite end forces, but the force arrows are hidden. Object X changes from 80.0 mm to 81.5 mm. Object Y changes from 60.0 mm to 58.8 mm. For each object, classify the loading and calculate the change in length. Then infer the direction of each pair of end forces and explain how both objects can remain stationary while deforming in opposite ways.

figure.purpose: Assess comparison of tension and compression in one view
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white diagram with two stationary horizontal objects X and Y and labelled original and final lengths. Omit force arrows and classification labels so learners infer both from the changes.
figure.alt_text: Stationary objects X and Y have labelled original and final lengths, with force arrows hidden.
